subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following characteristics do African apes and humans have in common?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
African apes and humans both have opposable thumbs, which is a shared primate characteristic.

subQuestions.questionText: Meiosis is a biologically important process because it …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Meiosis produces haploid gametes, which is essential for sexual reproduction and maintaining the chromosome number across generations.

options.B: doubles the chromosome number from generation to generation.

subQuestions.questionText: The reproductive isolation mechanism characterised by an animal displaying a specific action to attract a mating partner is known as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Species-specific courtship behaviour is a pre-zygotic reproductive isolation mechanism where animals display particular behaviours to attract mates of their own species.

options.A: breeding at different times of the year.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following genotypes is homozygous dominant?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
I^B I^B is homozygous dominant because it has two identical dominant alleles. RW shows codominance, Rr is heterozygous, and ii is homozygous recessive.

subQuestions.questionText: How many alleles control blood groups in humans?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Three alleles control blood groups in humans: I^A, I^B, and i (multiple allele inheritance).

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following is an example of discontinuous variation in humans?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Blood groups show discontinuous variation as individuals fall into distinct categories (A, B, AB, O) with no intermediates. Height, skin colour, and hair colour show continuous variation.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following is a CORRECT description of stem cells?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Stem cells are unspecialised cells that divide by mitosis to produce cells that may become specialised for specific functions.

options.A: Specialised cells that divide by mitosis to produce cells that may become further specialised for specific functions
options.B: Unspecialised cells that divide by mitosis to produce cells that may become specialised for specific functions
options.C: Unspecialised cells that divide by meiosis to produce cells that may become specialised for specific functions
options.D: Specialised cells that divide by meiosis to produce cells that may become specialised for specific functions

subQuestions.questionText:
A list of different lines of evidence to support evolution is given below.
(i) Evidence from biogeography
(ii) Fossil evidence
(iii) Genetic evidence
(iv) Cultural evidence
Which ONE of the following options are used as evidence to support human evolution?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Fossil evidence (ii), genetic evidence (iii), and cultural evidence (iv) all support human evolution. Biogeography is generally used for evolution in general but not specifically for human evolution in this context.

subQuestions.questionText: The police arrested two suspects accused of housebreaking. Their DNA profiles were analysed and compared to the profile of DNA evidence collected from the crime scene. (Refer to the DNA profile diagram in the question paper.) What conclusion can be drawn from the DNA analysis conducted by the police?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Neither of the suspects' DNA profiles match the DNA evidence from the crime scene, so neither suspect is positively linked to the crime.

options.A: Suspect 1 is positively linked to the crime.
options.B: Suspect 2 is positively linked to the crime.
options.C: Both suspects are positively linked the crime.
options.D: Neither of the suspects are positively linked to the crime.

subQuestions.memoText: Extinction (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The deliberate breeding of organisms for desirable characteristics selected by humans.
subQuestions.memoText: Artificial selection / Selective breeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: A genetic disorder characterised by the absence of a blood-clotting factor.
subQuestions.memoText: Haemophilia (1 mark)

subQuestions.memoText: Population (1 mark)

subQuestions.memoText: Autosomes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: A representation of the number, shape and arrangement of all the chromosomes in the nucleus of a somatic cell.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: 'The DNA-containing material in the nucleus of a non-dividing cell.' Column II: A: Chromatid; B: Chromatin.
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
Chromatin is the loose, uncoiled DNA-containing material in the nucleus of a non-dividing cell. Chromatids are formed from condensed chromatin during cell division.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: 'Location of DNA.' Column II: A: Nucleus; B: Mitochondria.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
DNA is found in both the nucleus (nuclear DNA) and the mitochondria (mitochondrial DNA).

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: 'The phase between two consecutive cell divisions.' Column II: A: Prophase; B: Telophase.
subQuestions.memoText:
None (2 marks)
The phase between two consecutive cell divisions is interphase. Prophase and telophase are both phases within cell division (mitosis or meiosis).

subQuestions.questionText: In a plant species, the gene coding for plant height has two alleles. The allele for tall plants (T) is dominant over the allele for dwarf plants (t). The gene for flower colour has two alleles where the allele for red flower colour (R) is dominant over the allele for white flower colour (r). A dwarf, white-flowered plant is crossed with a plant that is homozygous tall and heterozygous for red flower colour. State the characteristics that are being investigated in this cross.
subQuestions.memoText:
- Plant height (1 mark)
- Flower colour (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the genotype of the plant that is homozygous tall and heterozygous for red flower colour.
subQuestions.memoText:
TTRr (2 marks)
Mark 1: TT (homozygous tall)
Mark 2: Rr (heterozygous for red flower colour)

subQuestions.questionText: Below is an incomplete Punnett square representing the cross referred to above. (Punnett square: rows TR, Tr; column tr leading to offspring X, Y.) Identify the: (a) Genotype of offspring X; (b) Phenotype of offspring Y.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) TtRr (1 mark)
(b) Tall plant, white flower (2 marks)
Mark 1: Tall plant
Mark 2: White flower

subQuestions.memoText: Ovaries OR Testes (Mark first ONE only) (1 mark)

subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Spindle fibre (1 mark)
(b) Centriole / centrosome (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: How many chromosomes will be found in a somatic cell of this organism?

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE difference between the processes occurring in Diagram 1 and Diagram 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE difference (1 x 2 = 2 marks):

OR

subQuestions.questionText: The chromosomes in the diagram are genetically different due to crossing over. Describe the process of crossing over.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Adjacent (non-sister) chromatids of homologous chromosomes overlap
Mark 2: at points called chiasmata / chiasma
Mark 3: There is an exchange of genetic material

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how non-disjunction leads to Down syndrome.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Failure of a homologous pair 21 / chromosome 21 to separate
Mark 2: during Anaphase I / II
Mark 3: leads to a gamete with 24 chromosomes / an extra chromosome
Mark 4: The fertilisation of this gamete with a normal gamete / with 23 chromosomes
Mark 5: results in a zygote with 47 chromosomes / an extra chromosome / Trisomy 21

The mutation results in the amino acid proline (Pro) being replaced by arginine (Arg). Use the table and explain how this mutation will affect the protein that is synthesised.
subQuestions.memoText:

Mark 2: from CCT to CGT / second base in DNA triplet changed from C to G

Mark 4: The tRNA molecule with the anticodon CCU

Mark 6: The sequence of amino acids changes and
Mark 7: a different protein is formed

subQuestions.questionText: In some chickens, feather colour is controlled by two alleles, white feathers (W) and black feathers (B). If a homozygous white chicken is crossed with a homozygous black chicken, the offspring have feathers that are both black and white, a phenotype known as erminette. Explain why this inheritance is an example of co-dominance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Both alleles for black feathers and white feathers
Mark 2: are equally dominant / expressed in the phenotype of the erminette chicken

subQuestions.memoText: (Blood group) AB (1 mark)

subQuestions.memoText:
(*1 compulsory mark + any 5 = 6 marks)

P1 Phenotype: White x Erminette
Genotype: WW x BW
Meiosis ↓
Gametes: W, W x B, W
Fertilisation ↓
F1 Genotype: BW, WW, BW, WW

Marks awarded for:
- P1 phenotypes
- P1 genotypes

subQuestions.questionText: Hypophosphatemia is a sex-linked inherited condition caused by a dominant allele (X^H) on the X chromosome. The recessive allele (X^h) codes for normal phosphate levels. (Refer to the pedigree diagram in the question paper.) Name the type of: (a) Diagram shown; (b) Gonosome found only in males.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Pedigree diagram (1 mark)
(b) Y chromosome (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO effects of hypophosphatemia in humans.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Low levels of phosphate (in the blood)
Mark 2: can cause rickets
(Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.questionText: How many individuals in the F1-generation have hypophosphatemia?
subQuestions.memoText: 3 / Three (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ALL the possible genotypes of individual: (a) 3; (b) 4.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) X^h Y (1 mark)
(b) X^H X^h (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why ALL the daughters of individuals 1 and 2 will have hypophosphatemia.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 6 marks from:
- Individual 1 is a male with hypophosphatemia
- and has the genotype X^H Y
- The daughters inherit the dominant allele / X^H from their father
- Individual 2 is a female who does not have hypophosphatemia
- and has the genotype X^h X^h
- The daughters inherit one recessive allele / X^h from their mother
- The X^h from the mother / individual 2 is masked by the X^H from the father / all daughters will have X^H X^h genotype

subQuestions.questionText: Cloning is a process during which an identical copy of an organism is produced using biotechnology. Describe the process of cloning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 marks from EITHER:

Animals:
- The nucleus is removed from an ovum
- The nucleus of a donor somatic cell is removed
- and inserted into the ovum
- Electric shock is used to activate mitosis
- An embryo develops
- and is implanted into the surrogate mother

OR Plants:
- A plant with the desired characteristics is selected
- A vegetative part of the 'parent' plant structure is removed
- and placed inside a growth medium
- to supply nutrients / hormones
- to stimulate growth

subQuestions.questionText: List THREE benefits of cloning animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 marks from (Mark first THREE only):
- (Exact copies) of the most productive livestock are made
- (Exact copies) of animals with desired characteristics are made
- Conservation of endangered species
- Replacement of damaged tissues / organs

subQuestions.questionText: Read the extract about stickleback fish: Stickleback fish are small fish found in the ocean and freshwater lakes. Ocean ones have spikey fins for protection against predators. Until about 10 000 years ago, most stickleback fish lived in the ocean. After the last ice age, melting ice created new lakes and some populations swam into them. The connections between ocean and lakes dried up, trapping populations for thousands of years. Over time, the stickleback fish in the lakes lost the spikey fins. How would Lamarck have explained the absence of spikey fins on stickleback fish in lakes?
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 marks from:
- All stickleback fish had spikey fins originally
- In the lakes there were less / no predators
- The fish did not use the spikey fins anymore / they used their fins less
- and their spikes disappeared
- The acquired characteristic of no spikes was then passed on to the next generation
- Eventually all the fish had no spikes

- Skull A: Foramen magnum in a more backward position | Skull B: Foramen magnum in a more forward position

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage drug resistance in the blood samples taken. Show ALL working and round off your answer to ONE decimal place. (Total samples = 1 485, samples with malaria parasite = 551.)
State TWO ways in which the researchers ensured the following: (a) Validity of the investigation; (b) Reliability of the results.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Validity (Any TWO - Mark first TWO only) (2 marks):
- Blood samples only collected from people taking the antimalarial drug
- The same affected area of collection of blood samples
- The same villages were used for the investigation
- The same laboratory / environmental conditions where samples were kept

(b) Reliability (Any TWO - Mark first TWO only) (2 marks):
- Repeated three times
- Done in seven villages
- Duration over a year
- A sample of 1 485 was collected

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the malaria parasite developed drug resistance through natural selection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 7 marks from:
- There was variation in the malaria parasite population
- Some parasites were resistant to the antimalarial drugs and
- others were not
- When parasites were exposed to the antimalarial drugs
- Those that were not drug resistant did not survive / died
- Those that were resistant to the drugs survived and
- reproduced and
- passed the allele for drug resistance to their offspring
- The next generation had a higher proportion of parasites with drug resistance
